assets.title: 김서방의 보름가게
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original in-game screenshot concept mockup for a Korean-language article about a fictional 2D pixel-art management game, 16:9 landscape, full opaque canvas.
Primary request: a clearly playable shop-management moment in a Korean folklore world. Crisp, intentional pixel art with visible square pixels, coherent 16-bit sprite scale, warm and charming hanok roofs, hanbok clothing, paper lanterns and a huge full moon at a night festival. This is a game screen, not a poster.
Composition: elevated cross-section view into a small open-front wooden market stall. A human merchant in simple jade hanbok stands BEHIND the only checkout counter. Exactly three friendly horned dokkaebi customers wait in a clear left-to-right queue in front of that counter, each with one distinct order thought bubble: first a rice jelly cake, second straw sandals, third a folding hand fan. Small patience meters belong directly to these order bubbles. These are customer patience, never health meters. Three shelves behind the merchant visibly hold limited stock of these same three items.
Gameplay UI: top narrow status strip with a moon icon, coin icon and "120", "NIGHT 2", small clock icon. Bottom wide inventory panel contains exactly three large item slots with recognizable cake, sandals, fan icons, each displaying its quantity "2", "1", "3" and small coin price tags. Right side inset panel titled "RESTOCK" contains exactly three rows matching the items, quantity adjustment pictograms and cost numerals, with "BUDGET 120" at its bottom. A single item icon is being dragged from the cake inventory slot toward the customer at the register, showing the central allocation decision clearly. The artwork outside UI remains open and readable.
Lighting: amber lantern light against deep indigo night, friendly magical atmosphere, richly detailed but readable pixel art.
Text: only the short English labels listed above and minimal numerals, no large title, no Korean lettering, no paragraph text.
Constraints: all UI safely inside the frame; no cards or card deck; no combat, weapons, health bars or damage numbers; no 3D, photo, painterly smooth edges, logos, watermark, split-screen or promotional composition. Include full scene and readable gameplay controls.
assets.conversion: Pillow RGB conversion, nearest-neighbor resize to 1536x864, WebP quality 94 method 6; no redraw or content editing.

observed: Moonlit hanok market scene with full moon, lanterns, hanbok-clad shopkeeper behind one register, and exactly three horned dokkaebi customers.
Cake, straw sandals and fan appear as three distinct thought bubbles with patience meters.
Bottom inventory shows quantities 2, 1 and 3; each price is visible. Right RESTOCK panel contains three matching item rows and BUDGET 120.
Cake drag indicator and hand cursor communicate the immediate customer-service action.
No deck, weapon, battle, HP label or large title is present.
limitations: Concept UI is illustrative, not captured from a working game. Decorative shelf item counts are not a literal inventory tally. Customers are spread across the counter for readability rather than a physically strict single-file queue.

assets.title: 소류마 우편국
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original in-game screenshot concept mockup for a Korean-language article about a fictional 2D pixel-art automation logistics game, 16:9 landscape, full opaque canvas.
Primary request: a playable network scheduling and automated postal sorting screen in a warm Korean folklore village. Strict TOP-DOWN orthographic 2D tile map, intentional crisp square pixel art, coherent 16-bit game sprite scale; hanok buildings, stone walls, paddy grass, canal, Korean postal yard and small paper lanterns, daylight. This is an actual game screenshot composition, not a poster.
World layout: red mail sorting station on the left bank and blue mail sorting station on the right bank of a narrow vertical canal. One single-tile-wide wooden bridge in the center is the only crossing. Exactly THREE small wooden mechanical horse carriers with visible wooden jointed legs and colorful mailbags: one carries a red bag and occupies the bridge, one carries a blue bag waits immediately to the right of the bridge at a stop line, one carries another red bag waits immediately behind that blue carrier. Make these tiny folk automatons look like wooden horses, with no human riders.
Gameplay overlay: well-defined tiled paths form two looping delivery routes; red and blue transparent line overlays with frequent direction arrows show those routes, connecting sorting stations, bridge and the dock unloading station at the bottom right. Signal lamps at both ends of the bridge show one green reserved direction and one red stop direction; a small "1/1" capacity tag directly above the bridge. The dock has three visible marked mailbag unloading slots with one occupied. Colored mailbag icons on sorting belts and station counters. Use clear top-down spacing so the bridge bottleneck is immediately apparent.
UI: small top horizontal panel showing an envelope icon "24/min", throughput meter, and "IN TRANSIT 3". Bottom compact build toolbar with a road tile icon, a route-arrow icon, a stop-sign icon and a traffic-signal icon; selected signal tool outlined amber. On the upper right a small minimap and pause/speed controls "1x 2x". Only short English labels and numerals, no paragraph text, no big title.
Constraints: no combat, no cards, no hero avatar, no manual-driving dashboard; no isometric perspective, 3D, photographic textures, painterly smooth edges, logos or watermark; all UI safely inside frame; prioritize legible network scheduling and bridge reservation over decorative detail.
assets.conversion: Pillow RGB conversion, nearest-neighbor resize to 1536x864, WebP quality 94 method 6; no redraw or content editing.

observed: Top-down village tilemap with red and blue mail sorting areas separated by a canal and one central bridge.
Exactly three wooden horse carriers are visible: one on the bridge, two on the right approach; red and blue mailbags distinguish loads.
Bridge capacity 1/1, green and red reservation lights, colored route-arrow overlays, and a three-slot dock unloading area are visible.
Top UI shows 24/min and IN TRANSIT 3; bottom road, route, stop and signal icons are readable.
No character-driving controls, combat or deck interface is present.
limitations: Concept UI is illustrative, not captured from a working game. Some generated route arrows include mixed directions; the article rules, not decorative arrows, define the actual scheduling logic.
